title: Commitment Handshake: Provisioning Playbook for Dedicated Throughput and Autoscale Control
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Goal: Define an end-to-end operational playbook (intake form, automated checks, approval matrix, and capacity-plan artifacts) for provisioning Dedicated capacity commitments. The playbook ensures throughput guarantees are contractually documented, autoscaling policies are validated against workload profiles, and fleet controls (pinning, fallback tiers, and rollback) are exercised before commitment. Deliverables: intake form template, automated validation rules, approval checklist, SLA statement template, and a preflight simulator for capacity forecasts.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Intake form template available and validated by Solutions Eng (fields, required attachments, cost estimate)
2) Automated preflight checks implemented as a checklist (quota, region availability, model-compatibility, historical peak validation)
3) Approval matrix (auto-approve thresholds vs manual approvals) documented and signed off by Legal and Finance
4) Capacity plan artifact (CSV + visualization) produced for onboarding customers with >1M tokens/day
5) Playbook includes post-provisioning runbook: observability dashboard links, SLOs to monitor, and escalation steps
success_metrics: Mean time from request to provisioned: target < 5 business days for manual approvals, < 2 hours for auto-approve cases
Reduction in provisioning rework due to missing artifacts: target > 80% reduction
Accuracy of capacity forecast vs observed first 30 days: error < 15% for committed-throughput customers
implementation_notes: Intake form fields should capture: requested committed throughput (tokens/sec and tokens/day), expected 95th/99th percentile latency SLO, model family + quantization preference, preferred regions, expected traffic patterns (burst length & frequency), security posture (VPC/HSM), and billing contact
Auto-approve rules: requests <= baseline_region_capacity * 0.1 AND estimated monthly spend < $10k AND model in curated catalog => mark for auto-approve

Preflight simulator: use historical request shape sampling from similar customers to simulate latency and utilization given target fleet mix; integrated with fleet pricing model to produce cost delta for quantization and batching suggestions

Approval matrix: auto-approve, manager-approve (Product/SPMs), finance-approve (cost > threshold), legal-approve (enterprise contracts or custom SLA), infra-ops approver for specific hardware reservations
Autoscaling policy validation: require a baseline stress test (synthetic workload) that exercises burst-to-commitment transitions and validates burst buffer behavior and fallback policies
Fleet controls: commit document must record pinned model versions, allowed fallback variants, and mandatory rollback policy (e.g., rollback to previous stable model within 30 minutes on SLA breach)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (pilot): Run playbook with 3 existing enterprise customers (March) to gather missing edge cases
Phase 2 (automation): Implement auto-preflight checks in onboarding UI and wire approvals to workflow engine (April)
Phase 3 (scale): Expose standardized intake as API for channel partners; provide training and runbook to Sales/SE (May)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overly permissive auto-approve leads to commitments we cannot meet => Mitigation: conservative thresholds, holdback capacity pool, canary deployment requirement
Risk: Incomplete customer forecasts lead to undersized commitments => Mitigation: require historical traffic exports or minimum 30-day pilot; include penalty/true-up clauses in contract
Risk: Autoscale misconfiguration causes latency spikes => Mitigation: mandatory preflight stress test and staging window, circuit-breaker on rollout
Risk: Legal/regulatory delays on custom SLAs => Mitigation: templated SLA language and a documented escalation path with Legal
